meta.title: The Little Bird and the Camel
meta.textType: story: a traditional story with repeated lines

paragraphs: On Friday afternoon, Teacher Kim told the class a story. She had a big picture of a camel and a small bird. "Move your arms like wings when you hear the word hurry," she said. Lily and Mia moved their arms and laughed. The class sat on the floor and listened.

A little bird had nothing, and she had no nest. She flew over the sand for a long time. She was small, and her wings were tired. The sun was hot, and the desert was big. "I must find a place," she said. She asked a mouse, "Can I make my nest here?" "Not here," said the mouse. "It is too hot. Hurry, hurry, little bird!"

Next, she asked a tree. "Not here," said the tree. "The wind is too strong. Hurry, hurry, little bird!" The bird flew on and on. She was tired, but she did not stop. Then she saw a camel. "Can I make my nest on your back?" she asked. "I think that is a better idea," said the camel. "I go to the green place every day. We can go together."

The bird made a small nest of leaves on the camel's back. The camel walked slowly, and the bird sat in the nest. "Hurry, hurry, little bird!" said Teacher Kim, and the class moved their arms. The camel did not hurry, but the green place came near. There was water and a tall tree. The little bird looked at the sky and sang a song. "Now it is better," said the little bird. Teacher Kim smiled and said, "The end." Lily and Mia moved their arms like wings one more time.
